title: POC weekly: ops sprint ramp + secret-store handoff
next_steps: Redwood to send annotated benchmark spreadsheet and latency histogram by EOD Thu (Maya)
Arbor to confirm KMS key policy and SSO test account by next Monday (Zoë)
Diego to provision a staging route with prefix caching enabled and share curl sample (Diego, 2027-08-03)
Schedule canary traffic window for 2027-08-09, 90m slot (all)
action_items: Maya: Share table of dedupe and billing metrics from pilot (due 2027-07-30)
Diego: Provision gateway with VPC peering and KV cache enabled + sample client (due 2027-08-03)
Zoë: Send KMS policy and SOC2 scope questions (due 2027-08-02)
Priya: Validate SSO integration on staging account and report blockers (due 2027-08-04)
header: Date: 2027-07-29 | Time: 14:00-14:48 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ruiz, Riley Park (Redwood) — Priya Narang, Liam O'Connell, Zoë Mbaye, Adrian Chow (Arbor Analytics)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding velocity, access/gateway handoff for secret store/KMS, and preliminary benchmark interpretation. Action items center on KMS policy validation, Redwood provisioning of a staging gateway with KV/prefix cache, and sending annotated latency/cost artifacts. Customer raised SSO/KMS scope and a latency vs cost concern for tail p99s.
topics: Secret store / KMS handoff and audit log requirements
Staging gateway provisioning (VPC peering, routing, prefex/KV cache)
Preliminary benchmark results review and interpreting p50/p95/p99
Next steps for canary traffic and rollout window
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey team, thanks for taking time. Quick roll call — Maya here, Diego on the call for the infra bits, Riley joining for CSM support.
[00:12] Priya (Platform Eng): Hi all, Priya — Liam and Zoë from infra and sec are here too. Adrian from product on our side.
[00:20] Diego (Redwood SE): Morning. I'll jump into the provisioning checklist in a few minutes.
[00:28] Maya: Cool. Goal for today: confirm access handoff for secret store / KMS, review the small-run benchmarks we shipped yesterday, and line up the canary window.
[00:38] Liam (SRE): Quick note — we tried the staging route earlier and we hit an auth error, likely SSO. We'll detail in the ticket.
[00:45] Zoë (Security): And also want to validate token rotation and whether Redwood supports BYOK with our HSM.
[00:53] Maya: Totally. On BYOK, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — Diego can outline required IAM roles and the minimum policy. Diego?
[01:02] Diego: Yeah, for Redwood Private we request a minimal KMS decrypt key policy so the inference nodes can unwrap model artifacts and telemetry. You can restrict to service principal and we support key rotation. Note there is an audit log bucket requirement — we typically push audit metadata to the customer's audit S3 or provide an immutable log.
[01:22] Zoë: When you say "push audit metadata" — are we talking full request bodies or only metadata? We have strict PII rules.
[01:30] Diego: Good question. The default is metadata (timestamps, model id, route), not payload. Payloads are optional and require explicit opt-in and retention doc. We can sign an NDA addendum for the pilot if you need.
[01:44] Priya: That's acceptable — we'll avoid sending payloads. Need to confirm retention TTL for logs too.
[01:50] Maya: We'll include retention defaults in the artifact pack.
[01:54] [02:10] Speaker 1 (maybe Riley): I put a quick link to the benchmark sheet in chat, it's the annotated CSV with p50/p95/p99 and token counts — redwood.app/drive/benchmark-arn (note: link is placeholder).
[02:20] Priya: Saw that — thanks. We observed good p50 numbers but p99 spikes around 780ms which concerns the app team.
[02:28] Diego: Yep, looked at traces — the tail correlates with cold KV cache misses and long synthesis steps for long prompts. Two levers: increase prefix caching (reduce cold start), and bump the batching window slightly. That reduces cost savings a bit but improves tail latency.
[02:46] Liam: What's the unit cost impact if we enable heavier caching? We have budget constraints.
[02:52] Maya: Diego, do you have a ballpark?
[02:55] Diego: Rough estimate — enabling aggressive KV cache and keeping a warm pool reduces token compute by ~12% at 95% utilization but increases memory use and adds ~5-8% to fixed infra cost. For p99 reduction you trade off about 3-5% extra monthly. We'll add exact numbers to the annotated spreadsheet.
[03:18] Zoë: Also need to confirm encryption-at-rest for KV cache — is the cache encrypted with the same KMS key?
[03:25] Diego: Yes, we encrypt ephemeral caches at rest with customer KMS when Private, and for Dedicated we can enable in-transit encryption and disk-level encryption.
[03:34] Priya: Regarding the staging auth error — we created an OIDC app but the redirect URI didn't match. Is there a single-test account you recommend?
[03:42] Maya: We usually ask for a sandbox SSO/service account for integration testing. Riley, can we provide a minimal SSO test guide?
[03:48] Riley (CSM): Yep, I'll drop the checklist after the call — includes redirect URI, scopes, and test user creds.
[03:55] [04:12] Adrian (Product/Arbor): From product side, success criteria for the pilot: consistent p95 under 300ms for short prompts, <600ms for longer chains, and no escalations on security signoff. We'll probably need a 2-week canary.
[04:27] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We're aiming to hit those numbers with the staging config. Diego, what's the plan to get staging route up with VPC peering and secret store keys?
[04:35] Diego: I'll provision a staging gateway in Redwood Private that peeks into your VPC via peering. Need two items from Arbor: a VPC CIDR for peering and the KMS key ARN with the attached policy that allows Redwood service principal. Once we have that, we can spin up a small warm pool and enable KV prefix caching.
[04:55] Priya: We'll share the CIDR in the ticket. Is there a minimum subnet size?
[04:59] Diego: /24 is fine for the pilot. We'll document nimble network requirements in the guide.
[05:05] [05:30] Maya: Okay let's switch to benchmarks — we sent three small-run tests: baseline (no caching), caching enabled, and larger batch window. Priya, can you summarize what you saw?
[05:40] Priya: Baseline p50 ~120ms, p95 ~340ms, p99 ~780ms. Caching run p99 improved to ~420ms. Larger-batch run improved cost but p99 didn't move much.
[05:51] Diego: That matches expectation: batching reduces per-token cost but doesn't fix cold misses causing p99 outliers. Caching addresses the latter.
[06:00] Liam: Any chance the p99 is due to network hops between our region and the Redwood cluster? We are in eu-west-1 and your hosted cluster was in us-west-2 for the test.
[06:10] Diego: For the pilot we're proposing a dedicated pool in eu-west-1. In the staging tests the cross-region adds ~120-140ms, which would explain some tail. Once we place inference in your region, tail should drop.
[06:24] Zoë: Okay so the plan is region co-location + caching + warm pool. That should address p99—any fallback if we hit saturation?
[06:33] Maya: Our traffic router supports automated fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if the primary pool is saturated, with graceful degradation. We can tune the threshold.
[06:42] Priya: On quantized models — any quality regressions we should watch for?
[06:46] Diego: Small regressions mainly for low-temp open-ended tasks. We'll include evaluation prompts. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions against the prompt set.
[06:55] [07:22] Riley: Quick note — I added the eval prompt list to the shared doc.
[07:27] Priya: Great. Security question — you mentioned BYOK earlier, but what about HSM-backed keys and attestation?
[07:33] Diego: We support customer-provided keys in major cloud KMSes; if you require HSM attestation, we can integrate with your HSM provider but that goes into Private deployment territory and we'll need a slightly longer onboarding window. For the pilot you can use cloud KMS with a tight policy.
[07:52] Zoë: If we go Private, what additional logging/audit posture changes?
[07:58] Diego: Private gives you full control — you host the control plane in your VPC, logs routed to your buckets, and you can apply internal retention. We'll provide templates for SOC2 evidence collection.
[08:10] Maya: To keep pilot velocity, customers often start with dedicated/hybrid and then move to Private for full compliance.
[08:16] Adrian: Question on cost buckets — can you show us token-level billing broken down by route and model variant? We want clarity for showback.
[08:25] Maya: Yes, the console has token-level breakdown. Riley will add a sample export for your finance team.
[08:32] Riley: I'll attach the export format and a sample CSV.
[08:36] [09:00] Priya: Back to the staging error — Liam captured the OIDC mismatch and also a 403 from the KMS decryption when we attempted a test. Could be policy binding.
[09:09] Diego: Likely the service principal not present in the key policy. Zoë, if you can send the ARN and current key policy, I can propose the minimal delta.
[09:18] Zoë: Will do. Also curious about RBAC — does Redwood support fine-grained route-level RBAC?
[09:25] Maya: Yes, per-route RBAC and token scoping. You can create tokens scoped to a model or route and TTLs.
[09:32] Liam: Perfect. That helps our least-privilege needs.
[09:36] [10:02] Diego: I'll also add a small curl example showing how to call the staging gateway with prefix caching enabled and the sample token. That should help debug KMS errors quickly.
[10:10] Priya: Thanks. On the benchmarks, we'd like to see a histogram of request latencies rather than just p-values — helps to understand whether p99 is a few outliers or a heavy tail.
[10:19] Maya: Agreed; we'll include histograms in the follow-up artifact.
[10:24] Priya: Also can you annotate which runs were cross-region? We assume baseline was cross-region.
[10:29] Diego: Baseline was cross-region us-west-2 -> eu-west-1; caching run was us-west-2 with caching on but still cross-region; we'll re-run co-located tests once peering is done.
[10:42] Zoë: Regarding legal/procurement — we need a data processing addendum and the SOC2 report. Is SOC2 current?
[10:50] Maya: Yes, Redwood's SOC2 Type II report (most recent) and ISO summary are in the security share. I'll send the signed link after the call.
[10:58] Priya: Please include contact for security questionnaire follow-up.
[11:02] Maya: Riley will be the point.
[11:06] [12:00] Adrian: On timeline, if we clear staging access and KMS policy this week, can we aim for canary on 2027-08-09?
[12:09] Diego: Yes, provisioning and warm pool should take 48–72 hours once we have CIDR and key ARN.
[12:15] Maya: That gives us time to re-run localized benchmarks and finalize canary playbook.
[12:21] Priya: One blocker — our security team also wants to test key rotation during the pilot to ensure session continuity. Is that supported?
[12:28] Diego: We support key rotation; we'll run a rotation test in staging and observe unwrap behavior. There can be a brief reconnection window—I'll add steps to the runbook.
[12:38] Zoë: Please surface the exact window and rollback steps.
[12:44] Diego: Will do.
[12:47] [14:00] Riley: Quick ops housekeeping — I'll create the ticket linking the CIDR, KMS ARN, SSO test creds, and bench link. Expect it in ~30 minutes.
[14:05] Priya: Good. Also expect a short dataflow diagram? We need a diagram for procurement.
[14:11] Maya: We'll attach a network diagram and the data flow for audit.
[14:16] Liam: For fallback behavior — can we limit fallback to quantized variant only for non-critical routes?
[14:22] Diego: Yes, routes are configurable — you can set thresholds per route and exclude critical ones.
[14:27] Priya: Anything else on the runbook?
[14:30] Maya: We'll add a rollback playbook, health-check script, and the exact curl snippets for smoke tests.
[14:36] [15:00] Zoë: One last security point — are request headers redacted from logs by default? We want to ensure X-User and PII headers are stripped.
[15:08] Diego: Default scrub list excludes standard PII headers; you can provide a custom scrub list and we'll honor it for logs exported to your bucket.
[15:18] Priya: Great.
[15:22] Maya: Alright, recap of agreed next steps: Riley to post ticket with CIDR/KMS/SSO; Diego to provision staging sample and curl; Maya to send annotated benchmark histograms; Zoë to send key policy. Canary date targeted 2027-08-09.
[15:42] Priya: That's it from us. Thanks everyone.
[15:46] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up in Slack and ticket.
[15:50] [END]
